doc.title: Mandel Johnny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Keester Parade and Something Different
summary: Mandel jokes about the origins of Keester Parade and the deliberately stupid Something Different, which Bill Perkins recorded.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: That was a play on Easter Parade, keester was a very popular term amongst musicians in the 40s – 30s, 40s and 50s for a girls derrière.
It’s just as a simple blues basically.
The stupidest song I could ever think of, that should never have been recorded by anyone.

It was written to see how far you can stretch a stupid little motif, it was, if you could hear it the way I originally played it on the piano, you’d laugh. Bill Perkins actually made a record of it and I was totally aghast when he did it.
[laughs] Theme from MASH we talked about. “Where Do You Start?”
